column3: It repeats the Abrahamic charge to purify the House for circling, staying, bowing, and prostrating, directly expanding the focus's ordered worship space.
Its purified companions in lasting shade extend purification into a reward setting but do not clarify the House or its postures.
The ruined garden owner's regret at having associated partners supplies a concrete negative outcome for the focus's prohibition of association.
Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations, supplying the construction phase that precedes its purification and ritual use.
Its defended places where God's name is remembered extend the focus's cleared House into the need to preserve worship sites from demolition.
Its commands to bow, prostrate, worship, and do good directly restate the bodily worship sequence at the focus's purified House.
It explicitly identifies association with God as grave wrongdoing, directly defining the prohibition that guards the focus's center.
The immediately following call to proclaim pilgrimage turns the prepared House into an attended destination for people from afar.
Preparing stations for believers shows another deliberate arrangement of bodies in assigned places, though for battle rather than worship.
Its purification, fulfilled vows, and circling of the Ancient House continue the focus's ritual sequence and return it to the House.
The promise of gardens for believers does not add to the House, exclusive worship, or bodily ritual arrangement.
It directly condemns associating partners with God, reinforcing the exclusive allegiance required at the focus's House.
Entering a believer's house gives a domestic use of house language but adds little to the purified sanctuary and its rites.
Prepared dwellings carved from terrain show habitation as a granted and accountable spatial order, though not the focus's sanctuary.
Inheritance shares use partnership language in a legal sense unrelated to exclusive worship or the House.
Its identification of Abraham within an earlier righteous lineage only supplies a remote link to the focus's Abrahamic setting.
It gives the social practices of those established in the land, extending worship from the House into prayer, almsgiving, and moral order.
It contrasts the House's intended worship with empty ritual performed beside it, showing that proximity alone does not fulfill its purpose.
It establishes homes as a shared prayer direction for a threatened community, closely paralleling prepared dwelling space ordered for worship.
The pilgrimage benefits, remembrance, eating, and feeding of the poor extend the attendance announced after the focus into its communal ends.
The inhabited House offers only a brief parallel to the focus's House without its purification or worshippers.
Changing spouses and retaining a bridal gift do not clarify the House or its ritual order.
The preceding warning against barring access to the Sacred Mosque supplies the access condition for the House purified in the focus.
God's promise to settle persecuted migrants in a good place parallels prepared abode, but lacks the focus's ritual and House dimensions.
Praise after prostration extends devotion beyond the act itself, though it does not specify the House or bowing.
The adversary's approach from every direction does not clarify the focus's House, worshippers, or exclusive allegiance.
Circling between Hell and scalding water is a contrary, punitive motion and adds little after the focus's devotional circling.
Its commands to devote oneself, prostrate, and bow with those who bow closely parallel the focus's coordinated worship postures.
Collapsed unjust towns form a local contrast to the prepared and maintained worship place, but do not specify its rites.
Abandoned homes left by wrongdoing contrast with the focus's purified House as a dwelling kept functional through right use.
Joseph's ability to settle where he wills gives a broad parallel of granted placement without the House or worship sequence.
Inner blindness and travel through the land do not add to the focus's prepared sacred place or bodily worship.
Establishing prayer, giving alms, and bowing with others connects collective bodily worship to a broader sustaining practice.
It joins worship without association to concrete care for others, extending the focus's exclusive allegiance into social conduct.
Prepared elevated dwellings for believers provide a reward-side counterpart to the focus's assigned and purified place.
Its declaration that God is one and disavowal of association directly supports the focus's command not to associate anything with Him.
It names the Kaaba, the Sacred House, and associated rites as a sustaining order for people, directly illuminating the focus's House-centered arrangement.
Its universal prostration places the focus's human prostrators within a wider created order of submission.
Leaving a house by divine command concerns a different movement and does not clarify the focus's sacred House or rites.
Purification, prayer, almsgiving, and obedience make the household an ordered devotional space, though it is not the Sacred House.
A community standing in night recitation and prostration supplies a further collective pattern of the focus's upright and lowered worship.
The gathering and questioning of alleged partners exposes the accountability of association, directly supporting the focus's exclusion of partners.
It preserves kindness to parents while refusing pressure to associate partners with God, clarifying the priority of the focus's exclusive worship.
Its creation and resurrection signs do not clarify the House, its purification, or its worshippers.
It describes all in heaven and earth prostrating to God, extending the focus's prostration into comprehensive submission.
It repeats the refusal to obey even parental pressure toward association, reinforcing the focus's undivided allegiance.
The destruction of towns by sudden punishment does not add to the focus's sanctuary or bodily worship.
It declares that God has no partner in His rule, directly reinforcing the focus's ban on association.
The inability to answer the call to prostrate presents a judgment-day contrast to the available worship posture in the focus.
Adam and his spouse dwelling in the Garden do not clarify the House, purification, or worship sequence.
The attendants circling the blessed offer a distant motion parallel without the focus's House-centered worship.
Its protection of the Sacred House and pilgrims approaching it directly extends the focus's House into pilgrimage conduct and access.
Its warning against deviation regarding God's names gives a related boundary against corrupting divine exclusivity, but not the House or rites.
It rejects worship of others and the claim that they intercede with God, directly opposing the association barred in the focus.
It recalls people being called to prostrate while sound, framing the focus's postures as a present obligation rather than mere form.
Spending the night for God in prostration and standing directly joins two of the focus's ordered bodily positions.
The command that the angels prostrate after Adam's formation supplies a clear prostration scene, though with a different object and setting.
It combines secure establishment with worship of God without associating anything with Him, closely echoing the focus's placement and exclusivity.
Moses's collapse at the mountain supplies a different bodily response and does not clarify the House or prescribed worship.
The challenge to identify alleged partners makes their absence explicit, reinforcing the focus's command to exclude association.
The settlement of the Children of Israel gives a broad placement parallel but no House purification or ritual order.
Exile and punishment by fire do not add to the focus's House, devotion, or exclusive worship.
Joseph invokes Abraham's lineage while declaring that no association with God is permissible, directly reinforcing the focus's Abrahamic command.
Bearing sin and entering the Fire does not clarify the House or the focus's worship sequence.
The statement that God does not will injustice for the worlds does not add to the focus's spatial or ritual content.
It explicitly rejects associating anyone with the Lord, directly restating the focus's exclusive allegiance.
A caller from a near place does not clarify the focus's prepared House or its rites.
Faith, moral command, and haste toward good offer a broad devotional extension but do not specify the House or its postures.
Movement among those who prostrate gives a compact prostration link, though without the focus's House or full ritual sequence.
Grasping from a distant place does not clarify sacred placement, purification, or worship.
The staff's frightening movement and Moses's retreat do not add to the focus's House or ritual bodies.
Reconciliation between fighting believers does not clarify the focus's sacred place, purification, or postures.
Its believers are repeatedly described as bowing and prostrating while seeking God's favor, directly paralleling the focus's worshippers.
The expulsion and self-destruction of homes contrast with prepared dwelling, but add little to the focus's sacred ritual use.
Pilgrimage to the House and circling the two landmarks directly extend the focus's House-centered circling into pilgrimage practice.
Faith in God and the messenger does not clarify the House, purification, or bodily worship sequence.
The magicians fall prostrate, providing an immediate embodied response of submission though outside the House setting.
God's justice and human self-wronging do not add to the focus's sacred place or its rites.
Remembering revelation recited in homes makes a household a site of learning, but it does not clarify the purified House or postures.
Replacing one sign with another does not clarify the focus's House, exclusive worship, or ritual bodies.
Iblis's refusal to prostrate gives a clear contrary boundary to the willing bowing and prostration ordered in the focus.
Its description of something raised and purified offers only a lexical purification link without House or worship context.
The deniers' false claim that they were not associators exposes the accountability of the very association forbidden in the focus.
Claims that homes are exposed serve as an excuse for retreat and do not clarify the focus's sacred House or rites.
The angels' complete prostration provides another scene of undivided bodily obedience, though not at the House.
Their refusal when told to bow supplies a direct negative contrast to the focus's commanded bowing worshippers.
Sharing punishment uses partnership language in a different sense and does not illuminate the focus's prohibition of association.
The refusal to purify certain hearts offers a distant contrast to the focus's purification of the House, without its ritual setting.
Entering by a gate in prostration links bodily humility with access to a place, though not to the House or its full sequence.
Disbelief and claims about the unseen from afar do not clarify sacred placement or worship.
Its faith, prayer, giving, and covenant keeping give a broad account of righteousness but add little after the direct House and posture parallels.
It challenges association with God without revealed authority, directly sharpening the focus's demand for undivided worship.
The divided tribes and their provision do not clarify the House, purification, or bodily ritual.
Iblis explicitly refuses to prostrate to a human, offering a focused contrast to the obedient postures in the focus.
The bare denial of refuge does not add to the House, association, purification, or worship sequence.
Iblis questions prostrating to Adam, again setting refusal against the focus's ordered bodily submission.
Working from one's position and awaiting the outcome does not clarify the focus's prepared House or rites.
Its direct command to prostrate to God and worship Him succinctly restates the focus's devotional end.
Its rules for eating in family homes concern domestic access rather than the purified sacred House or its worshippers.
It denies that God has a partner in sovereignty and commands His exaltation, directly reinforcing the focus's exclusive worship.
Abraham and Ishmael ask to be shown their rites, directly supplying the ritual instruction that complements the focus's House and worshippers.
It identifies the first House established for humanity at Bakkah, directly clarifying the unique House assigned to Abraham in the focus.
The secure House, Abraham's standing place, and pilgrimage duty directly expand the focus's prepared sanctuary and its attended worship.
Following Abraham's upright religion and taking him as a close friend supplies an Abrahamic monotheism frame for the focus.
It identifies Abraham's upright way as free of association, reinforcing the focus's Abrahamic command against associating partners.
It denies associators the right to maintain God's mosques, directly joining exclusive faith to the care of sacred worship space.
It describes those who maintain God's mosques through faith, prayer, almsgiving, and fear of God, extending the focus's purified House into sustained practice.
Service to pilgrims and the Sacred Mosque is distinguished from faith and striving, clarifying that sanctuary service requires more than a public role.
It bars associators from approaching the Sacred Mosque, directly protecting the exclusive worship and purity ordered at the focus's sanctuary.
Abraham asks for a secure city and protection from idol worship, closely joining his sacred settlement to the focus's ban on association.
Abraham settles his descendants near the Sacred House so that they may establish prayer, directly linking the House's location to its worship function.
It explicitly calls Abraham upright and not among the associators, directly strengthening the focus's Abrahamic monotheism.
The Sacred Mosque anchors the night journey, confirming its distinctive sacred status though not its purification or ritual sequence.
Abraham's household is guided to good deeds, prayer, almsgiving, and worship, extending the focus's Abrahamic setting into a sustained devotional order.
Honoring sacred ordinances and avoiding idolatrous falsehood directly continue the focus's purified sanctuary and exclusive allegiance.
It commands upright devotion to God without association, directly restating the focus's central prohibition within the same pilgrimage passage.
Honoring God's rites continues the focus's sacred-place logic by locating their reverence in piety of the hearts.
The prescribed rites, naming God, and submission to the one God extend the focus's bodily worship into sacrificial devotion and monotheism.
The humbled believers who establish prayer and give from provision extend the focus's worshippers into a durable ethical and devotional disposition.
Sacrificial animals are made among God's rites and His name is pronounced over them, extending the focus's House service into pilgrimage sacrifice.
It distinguishes piety from the outward flesh and blood of sacrifice, clarifying the inward purpose of the rites surrounding the focus.
A prescribed rite for every community provides a broader frame for the specific House-centered ritual order in the focus.
It names Abraham's religion and commands prayer, almsgiving, and holding fast to God, directly extending the focus's Abrahamic worship order.
It describes houses raised for God's name to be remembered in them, closely paralleling the focus's House purified for worship.
Its worshippers maintain remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving despite commerce, extending sacred-space worship into steadfast daily practice.
Abraham's command to worship God and fear Him supplies a direct Abrahamic call to exclusive devotion, though without the House.
It warns that association nullifies deeds, sharpening the consequence of violating the focus's command not to associate anything with God.
It commands prostration to God rather than sun or moon, directly clarifying that the focus's prostration is exclusive divine worship.
It describes opponents barring believers from the Sacred Mosque and their offerings, directly complementing the focus's House with its threatened access.
Abraham and those with him disavow the worship of others until belief in God alone, reinforcing the focus's Abrahamic exclusivity.
It declares that places of prostration belong to God and forbids calling on anyone alongside Him, directly joining sacred space to exclusive worship.
It commands sincere worship of God alone together with prayer and almsgiving, directly restating the focus's unshared devotional order.
Its declaration that God is One provides a concise theological ground for the focus's prohibition of association.
It denies that anything is comparable to God, directly reinforcing the exclusive allegiance that preserves the focus's center.
